headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: transformers can write/run code and egress broadly, while ai-engineering-hub is an unverified docs-only agent with no isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented I/O surfaces, but B reads files, runs browsers, and processes stdin/stdout, so if A’s outputs are copied into B’s workspace or prompts, injected instructions could be followed. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation. Uncertainty about A’s actual runtime surface pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A’s outputs are copied into B’s stdin/stdout or files without sanitization
IF B is configured to treat file contents as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt
Strip executable directives from A’s outputs before passing to B
Use a read-only handoff file with provenance labels
Disable browser/tool execution for B on A-derived content
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read and write the filesystem and egress broadly, while A’s docs-only profile does not prove any data handling limits. If they share a workspace, B can exfiltrate files or intermediate artifacts that A touches. Because A’s data classes are unspecified, this is an inferred but plausible default-path leakage risk.
conditions: IF A and B share any writable workspace or mounted directory
IF B is given access to files produced by A
mitigations: Place each agent in separate directories
Remove network egress from B during shared runs
Mount A’s workspace read-only for B
Scan handoff files for secrets before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and package-install capabilities; A is an agent repository with no documented locking or runtime constraints. If both operate on the same repo or directory, concurrent writes can corrupt files or overwrite each other. Because B supports multiple instances and no lock is documented, the default conflict pathway is dangerous.
conditions: IF A and B are pointed at the same writable directory
IF B runs more than one instance against shared state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Disable package installs during shared edits
Use git branches per agent
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume files and stdout from A, and B’s pipeline-style tool use suggests it may act on upstream outputs. A is docs-only and unverified, so any mistaken facts or malformed instructions from A can cascade into B’s downstream processing. The pathway exists in default integration patterns, though not every deployment will wire them together.
conditions: IF B uses A’s output as an input document or prompt
IF B performs downstream actions without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B acts on A’s output
Require citations for any factual claims passed downstream
Use a human review gate for high-impact actions
Log and diff A-to-B handoffs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both are open-source docs-only profiles. The only concrete compliance concern is that B can process multimodal data and egress broadly, but A does not declare regulated data classes. This is a limited, documentation-gap risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared workflow
IF B is used in a jurisdictional or retention-sensitive deployment
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Document retention and deletion settings
Restrict B’s egress for sensitive runs
Tag inputs by data class before processing
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
